I am a woman of 42 years, farming this small sorghum plot here in the North West. The land belongs to my household, so I will put my effort into it. I will intercrop with cowpea as we always do, to help the soil and feed my family. I cannot afford much, but I will try to buy a small bag of urea from the market when the rains come steady, and I will carry manure from our goats and chickens to spread before planting. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest — it grows well here and I trust it. For the weeds, my children and I will hoe, and I may buy a little herbicide if the money is there after planting. There is no irrigation here; we depend on God and the rain.
